# Taxonomy of Grid-Based Logic Games

## Primary Classification by Core Mechanic

---

## 1. LOOP-DRAWING GAMES
*The primary goal is to draw a single continuous closed loop*

### 1.1 Unconstrained Path Loop
Games where the loop may pass freely through any eligible cell

- **Slitherlink** — Loop drawn between dots; numbers indicate how many sides of a cell are used
- **Masyu** — Loop must pass through all circles; black/white circles impose turn/straight rules
- **Yajilin** — Loop avoids black cells; arrow-numbers indicate black cell counts in a direction

### 1.2 Constrained Cell-Type Loop
Games where specific cells impose strict movement rules

- **Dotchi-Loop** — Loop passes through white circles; within each bold-line area, all circles must be treated uniformly (all straight or all turning)
- **Moon-or-Sun** — Loop passes through rooms once; must alternate between moon-only and sun-only rooms
- **Mid-loop** — Loop must pass through black circles with the circle as the exact midpoint of a straight segment
- **Nagareru** — Loop direction constrained by wind arrows in black cells; cannot move against wind

### 1.3 Gated/Structured Loop
Games where the loop interacts with structural elements beyond cells

- **Suraromu** — Loop starts/ends at a numbered circle; must pass through all "Gates" exactly once in a specified order

---

## 2. PATH & CONNECTION GAMES
*The primary goal is to draw paths or connections between specific points (not necessarily forming a loop)*

### 2.1 Island Connection
- **Hashiwokakero** — Connect numbered islands with bridges; bridge count must match island number; all islands form one connected network

### 2.2 Pair Connection
- **Numberlink** — Connect matching number pairs with non-crossing, non-branching lines that fill the grid

### 2.3 Movement/Migration
- **Satogaeri** — Move circles horizontally or vertically into their home country; paths cannot cross
- **Yosenabe** — Move numbered circles into gray areas; arrow paths cannot cross; gray area totals must match

---

## 3. REGION DIVISION GAMES
*The primary goal is to partition the grid into defined regions or blocks*

### 3.1 Division into Uniform Rectangles/Squares
- **Shikaku** — Divide grid into rectangles; each rectangle contains exactly one number equal to its cell count

### 3.2 Division into Polyominoes
- **Fillomino** — Divide grid into blocks where each block's size equals its number; same-sized blocks cannot touch
- **LITS** — Color exactly four cells (tetromino) per bold-line region; same-shaped tetrominoes cannot touch; colored cells must connect; no 2×2 colored squares
- **Norinori** — Place dominoes (pairs of consecutive black squares) in regions; each region gets exactly two black squares
- **Five Cells** — Divide grid into pentominoes (blocks of exactly five cells); numbers indicate how many block-boundary lines surround a cell

### 3.3 Division into Specialized Shapes
- **Sashigane** — Divide grid into L-shaped blocks; circles mark the bend; arrows point toward the bend from an end
- **Double Choco** — Divide grid into blocks each containing equal white and gray areas of identical shape (possibly rotated/mirrored)

### 3.4 Division with Evolving/Sequential Blocks
- **Evolomino** — Blocks grow sequentially along arrow paths, each subsequent block adding one square to the previous shape

---

## 4. CELL-SHADING / PAINTING GAMES
*The primary goal is to determine which cells to color black (or shade)*

### 4.1 Shading with Connectivity Constraints
- **Nurikabe** — Shade cells to form a connected black "wall"; white cell islands each contain exactly one number equal to island size; no 2×2 black squares
- **Heyawake** — Shade cells in rooms per given counts; shaded cells cannot connect; white cells cannot span more than two rooms in a line
- **Hitori** — Shade cells so no number repeats in any row or column; shaded cells cannot touch; white cells stay connected
- **Kurodoko** — Shade cells so numbered white cells count visible white cells in four directions correctly; black cells cannot touch; white cells stay connected

### 4.2 Shading with Shape Constraints
- **Choco Banana** — Black regions must be rectangles/squares; white regions must not be rectangles/squares; numbers indicate region size
- **Usowan** — Shade cells per adjacency counts, but exactly one number per bold-line rectangle is intentionally wrong; shaded cells cannot connect; white cells stay connected
- **Kurotto** — Shade cells; numbered circles indicate total adjacent black cells in all four directions; circles cannot be shaded

### 4.3 Shading with Structural/Gravity Rules
- **Sto-stone** — Shade cells in rooms per given counts; when "dropped" downward, shaded cells must fill exactly the bottom half of the grid

### 4.4 Shading to Reveal an Image
- **Tilepaint** — Color entire tiles (bold-line regions) based on diagonal-cell counts for rows/columns; solution reveals a recognizable object

### 4.5 Shading with Triangle Placement
- **Shakashaka** — Place black triangles in cells so remaining white areas always form rectangles/squares; numbers indicate adjacent triangle count

### 4.6 Shading with Block-Chain Rules
- **Chained Block** — Shade cells into blocks; each block contains one number or "?"; blocks must form chains (corner-touching); no two same-shaped blocks in one chain

### 4.7 Shading with Twin-Block Rules
- **Nuritwin** — Shade cells so each bold-line region contains exactly two same-sized blocks; blocks in same region cannot touch; all shaded cells connect globally; no 2×2 shaded squares

---

## 5. NUMBER-PLACEMENT GAMES
*The primary goal is to fill cells with numbers according to logical constraints*

### 5.1 Latin Square / Uniqueness Constraint
- **Sudoku** — Place 1–9 in each cell; each row, column, and 3×3 box contains all digits once

### 5.2 Region-Based Number Filling
- **Ripple Effect** — Fill rooms with consecutive numbers from 1; duplicate numbers in a row/column must be separated by at least that number of cells
- **Makaro** — Fill rooms with 1 through room-size; arrow black cells indicate which neighbor holds the largest value; same numbers in different rooms cannot be adjacent

### 5.3 Snake/Sequence Placement
- **Hebi** — Place snake segments numbered 1–5 sequentially in white cells; snakes cannot touch; line-of-sight rules prevent snakes from "attacking" each other

### 5.4 Crossword-Style Number Placement
- **Nansuke** — Fill blank white cells with digits from a given number list; numbers read left-to-right or top-to-bottom

---

## 6. SYMBOL/MARK PLACEMENT GAMES
*The primary goal is to place specific non-numeric symbols or marks in cells*

### 6.1 Light/Illumination Placement
- **Akari** — Place light bulbs in white cells; numbered cells indicate adjacent bulb count; every white cell must be illuminated; bulbs cannot illuminate each other

### 6.2 Directional Mark Placement
- **Juosan** — Fill every cell with "—" or "|"; territory numbers indicate the difference in mark counts; horizontal marks cannot stack more than two rows; vertical marks cannot span more than two columns

### 6.3 Square/Block Placement with Growth Rules
- **Evolomino** *(also classifiable here)* — Place squares along arrow paths; each successive block grows by one cell without rotation or flipping

---

## 7. MAZE & ROUTING GAMES
*The primary goal involves creating or navigating a maze structure*

- **Nurimeizu** — Paint rooms to create walls forming a maze from S to G; circle cells must lie on the shortest path; triangle cells must not; no 2×2 painted or unpainted squares; white cells cannot form a loop

---

## 8. HYBRID / MULTI-MECHANIC GAMES
*Games combining two or more primary mechanics in roughly equal measure*

### 8.1 Shading + Loop
- **Yajilin** *(also in Loop)* — Determine black cell placement via arrow clues AND draw a loop through remaining cells

### 8.2 Division + Shading
- **Nurimisaki** — Shade cells while preserving "promontory" white circles (each with exactly one white neighbor); numbered circles specify white-cell line length; white cells must connect; no 2×2 uniformly colored squares

### 8.3 Path + Shading
- **Nurimeizu** *(also in Maze)* — Combines room-shading decisions with shortest-path routing logic

### 8.4 Loop + Shading
- **Dotchi-Loop** *(also in Loop)* — Loop interacts with pre-placed black circles (avoided) and white circles (traversed with uniformity rule)

### 8.5 Number Placement + Region Division
- **Fillomino** *(also in Region Division)* — Numbers both define and are placed within regions simultaneously

### 8.6 Movement + Number Totaling
- **Yosenabe** *(also in Path)* — Combines directional movement of numbered pieces with arithmetic sum constraints on destination areas

---
